text.p: Swiss shares ended on a positive note on average volumes, with the market following pharmaceuticals, which made a strong showing.
Some dealers were surprised with the market's gains. Others said the upward move may have stemmed from a reaction to Thursday's losses, follow-through buying or gains on the London stock exchange.
Special situations and the trend on Wall Street were seen as the main factors for Swiss shares in coming session.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index closed 21.3 points, or 0.55 percent, higher at 3,882.8 and the broad SPI added 12.16 points to end at 2,481.59.
There was talk in the market that Ciba and Sandoz, which plan to merge to form Novartis, would soon get approval from U.S. authorities, dealers said.
Ciba registereds rose more than one percent to 1,592. Sandoz added 0.8 percent to 1,496. Roche certificates, which led the actives list, were up 70 francs to 10,020.
UBS bearer shares were also sought. They closed unchanged at 1,265. One trader said the market's curiosity ahead of Tuesday's UBS news conference was growing.
Analyst expected UBS, Switzerland biggest bank, to unveil plans for cutting costs but without dramtic job cuts.
SBC added 2.25 francs to close at 256.25.
